one_month_reasoning: Two scheduled events fall inside the 2026-10-09 to 2026-11-08 window. (1) Q3 2026 results, which Alpha Vantage lists for 2026-11-04 as an estimate (src 3). Paycom had not announced the date as of 2026-10-11; last year's Q3 came out on Nov 5 after the close. Consensus Q3 non-GAAP EPS is $2.79 (src 2). Paycom beat Q2 by about 17% ($2.78 vs $2.38, src 1/2), and since then three things have helped: a further ~2.6M shares were bought back in Q2 (src 1), the Fed hiked in September (Polymarket 'rate hike by Sep 2026 meeting' resolved Yes, src 13), which lifts float income above a $105M guide that assumed flat rates (src 6), and LinkedIn headcount fell another ~5% over the summer (src 8). So I expect a beat and probably a small guide raise. Against that, the stock nearly doubled from April to August (src 7), sits above the average analyst target of $220 (src 5) and has already priced in a lot. The reaction is two-sided and large: the Q2 print moved the stock about +21% intraday (src 7). (2) The FOMC meeting on Oct 27-28. Polymarket prices no change at 83.5% and +25bp at 16.5%, with $8.5M and $7.2M traded (src 13). A hike would help float income but hurt the multiple, so I treat it as roughly neutral. Net: the distribution is centred slightly above spot (median about $234) with a monthly sigma of about 16%. That is wider than the 46%/3.5 = 13% base because an earnings print falls inside the window.

fair_value.method: A blend of 60% P/E and 40% DCF, valued at Oct 2027. P/E: NTM EPS of $15.11 (a blend of FY27 consensus $13.95 and my FY28 estimate of $15.50) x 17.0x gives $257. DCF: 2027 FCF of $700M less a $60M SBC haircut, FCF growing 8% down to 4%, a 9.5% discount rate, 3% terminal growth, $702M net debt and 41.5M shares gives $268. Blend = $261.

bear.story: Recurring growth slows to about 5%. The newly hired reps ramp slowly. AI-driven headcount cuts at clients shrink per-employee billing, and AI-native rivals win share. The Fed reverses to cuts and float income falls. Leverage from the $900M revolver becomes a talking point. EPS stalls near $13 and the multiple drops to about 12.5x, roughly the Simply Wall St 14.1x future P/E with a haircut: about $165.

base.story: Revenue grows 7-8%, EBITDA margin holds at about 46%, and buybacks continue from FCF of more than $650M. FY27 EPS comes in around $14 and NTM EPS around $15 by Oct 2027, valued at about 17x like Paychex and Paylocity: about $255.

bull.story: The expanded sales force (job posts up 52% in 3 months, 90% sales and delivery) and IWant/automation lift recurring growth back to 10% or more. Margins pass 48% as headcount keeps falling. Rates stay higher. NTM EPS of about $16 at roughly 20x gives about $325, still below ADP's 22x.

comps_summary.peer_range: Forward P/E 7.6x (ASUR) to 22.1x (ADP), median 16.2x. EV/EBITDA 10.1x (ASUR) to 63.7x (NSP), median 15.2x. The EV/EBITDA figures are trailing (TTM) as published by StockAnalysis, which shows no forward EV/EBITDA; I place them in the ev_ebitda_fwd field for lack of a sourced forward figure. Dayforce was taken private on 2026-02-04 and Alight's data look broken, so both are excluded. Paycor (acquired by Paychex), UKG, Rippling, Deel and Gusto are unlisted, so only 10 genuine listed comps exist.
comps_summary.our_multiple_vs_peers: 17.0x forward P/E: about 0.8x above the 16.2x median and inside the range, between PAYX (17.2x) and PCTY (17.6x). PAYC itself trades at 17.7x forward and 15.1x TTM EV/EBITDA against a 15.2x peer median.
comps_summary.premium_discount_justification: No premium is claimed. PAYC's 46% EBITDA margin guide (src 1) matches Paychex at 46.6% EBITDA margin, and its 7-8% revenue growth matches Paylocity's 7.3% forecast, so I put it with those two. PAYC's faster EPS growth (+15% in 2027) comes mainly from buybacks funded partly by debt, which I do not count as structural. Founder/key-person risk and the AI seat-compression debate argue against a premium.

thesis_break_reason: $160 is the lowest Street target (src 5) and about 11.5x FY27 consensus EPS, well below every payroll peer but ASUR. Reaching it would most likely mean the EPS path itself has broken: recurring growth below about 5%, a failed sales-force ramp, visible client seat compression from AI, or a forced slowdown in buybacks or a debt problem. Ordinary de-rating would not get there. Trading there would also put the stock back to roughly its mid-2026 level, before the Q2 beat and raise.

key_uncertainties: Whether the enlarged sales force ramps. Job posts are up 52% in 3 months and 90% are sales and delivery roles (src 9); management flagged ramp risk (src 6).
AI seat compression: clients cutting headcount reduces per-employee billing, and AI-native HCM entrants compete for new logos.
Rate path. A September 2026 hike helps float income; cuts in 2027 would cut the ~$105M line (src 6, 13).
Leverage-funded buybacks: $900M drawn on a $2.1B revolver and cash down to $198M (src 1, 7). EPS growth is partly financial engineering.
Quality of alt data: LinkedIn headcount and job-post scrapes are estimates. Reddit, X, Glassdoor, Indeed, G2 and TrustRadius were blocked, so customer sentiment is thin.
reasoning: Facts: Q2 2026 beat by about 17% on EPS ($2.78 vs $2.38). Revenue was $531M (+9.8%), recurring revenue +11%, adjusted EBITDA margin 44.2%. FY26 guidance was raised to $2.197-2.212B revenue and about 46% EBITDA margin. Shares fell from 56.1M to 44.3M after $1.39B of H1 buybacks, partly funded by a $900M revolver draw (src 1, 7). Consensus FY26/FY27 EPS is $12.09/$13.95, revised up about 13% over 60 days (src 2). The Street is lukewarm: median target $210, 13 of 21 Hold, against a $232 price (src 5). Alternative-lane evidence: (a) LinkedIn headcount fell 12% from April to September 2026, 6,274 to 5,541 (src 8). This independently backs management's AI automation and R&D savings story (src 6, 7) and makes the 46% margin guide look credible to beat. (b) LinkedIn job posts are up 52% over 3 months, 90% in sales and delivery (src 9). This independently confirms the sales-force expansion management described (src 6) and is a leading indicator for 2027 bookings that consensus revenue (+7.4%) may not yet reflect. (c) Web traffic is flat at -0.7% over 3 months (src 10), so there is no demand acceleration yet. (d) The Paycom app holds 4.8 stars on 1.6M ratings at #45 in Business versus ADP at #9 (src 11, 12), showing a stable user base with no sign of churn. (e) Polymarket shows the Fed hiked in September and prices only 2.3% for a cut by December (src 13), a tailwind to float income relative to guidance. (f) The Simply Wall St community narrative cut its fair value to $195 on a 14.1x P/E (src 14), a useful bearish anchor. Reddit, X, Glassdoor, Indeed, G2 and TrustRadius all blocked fetching; I did not work around them. Valuation: P/E at 17x NTM EPS of $15.11 gives $257; DCF gives $268; the 60/40 blend is $261. Scenarios: $165/$255/$325 at 22/53/25%, a mean of about $253. Ladder: lognormal with a median of about $243 (slightly above spot: fair value is about 12% above, offset by mean reversion after a 98% rally and a Street median below spot). Sigma is about 0.38, below the 46% realized volatility, which was inflated by the crash-and-recovery year; the left tail is fattened for leverage and AI risk. Lane accounting: 8 of 25 sources are in-lane (32%), below the 60% target. The shortfall is because the mandatory 10-peer comp set needed 10 data pages; excluding those, 8 of 15 (53%) are in-lane. Six in-lane sources (src 8-13) are ones other lanes are unlikely to find. Research was limited: Twelve Data and most Alpha Vantage endpoints were plan- or rate-limited, and the Q3 report date is an estimate.
